'''Umotína''' or '''Umutína''' is a recently extinct [[Bororoan languages|Bororoan language]] of Brazil.<ref name="Schultz, 1952">{{Cite journal |last=Schultz |first=Harald |date=1952 |title=Vocabulario dos Indios Umutina. |url=https://www.persee.fr/doc/jsa_0037-9174_1952_num_41_1_2400 |journal=Journal de la société des américanistes |volume=41 |issue=1 |pages=81–137 |doi=10.3406/jsa.1952.2400}}</ref> As of 2015, only two elders remembered the language.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Cruz |first=Mônica Cidele |last2=Corozomae |first2=Marcio Monzilar |date=2015-07-12 |title=O ENSINO DE LÍNGUA MATERNA NA ESCOLA INDÍGENA JULÁ PARÉ |url=https://periodicos.unemat.br/index.php/ecos/article/view/692 |journal=Revista ECOS |language=pt |volume=18 |issue=1 |issn=2316-3933}}</ref> The language was decimated by various epidemics among the Umutina.<ref name="PIB" />

==Phonology==

=== Consonants ===
It is one of the few languages in the world reported to have a [[linguolabial consonant]]: In unpublished data, [[Floyd Lounsbury]] recorded a [[voiceless linguolabial plosive]] {{IPAblink|t̼}}.<ref name="Martin, 1956" /><ref name="Olson et al., 2013" />
